/itineraryStops/5/description.source_en:
**Jeju Haenyeo (women divers) culture** is a living heritage inscribed on the **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list in 2016**. On this tour you don't watch a museum display but **a real haenyeo diving performance staged in the sea below ⟦G1⟧**. **Elderly, still-active haenyeo** who have made the sea their workplace their whole lives free-dive without oxygen gear, relying on a *tewak* (float), and you can hear for yourself the distinctive whistling sumbisori breath they release when they finish a dive. 

The performance usually runs **twice a day (around 13:30 and 15:00)**, depending on sea and weather conditions, and **viewing is free**. Haenyeo are divided into **hagun, junggun, and sanggun** by depth and diving ability, with the sanggun descending **more than 10 m on a single breath**. Fewer than **4,000 haenyeo are active today, most of them over 70**, so every scene of diving you witness in person is a record of a vanishing heritage. 

**On days when the performance is canceled due to weather or waves**, we substitute the **⟦G0⟧** in Hado-ri, Gujwa-eup (₩1,100 for adults, about 80% indoors, three exhibition halls), continuing the same UNESCO intangible heritage in depth, indoors.

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Performance usually 13:30 and 15:00 (varies with the day's sea and weather) / Haenyeo Museum 09:00–18:00 (last entry 17:00)

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/closed.source_en: Performance: canceled in bad weather or waves / Museum: closed Mondays, January 1, Lunar New Year, Chuseok

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Easy — viewed from the shore; if substituted with the museum, fully indoor with elevators

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Diving performance viewing free / if substituted, Haenyeo Museum adult ₩1,100 · teens ₩800 · children ₩500

/itineraryStops/6/category.source_en: UNESCO World Natural Heritage — Geomunoreum Lava-Tube System (inscribed 2007)

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/1.source_en: Descent into the second entrance + entering the cave — about 5 min

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/2.source_en: 1 km open-section round trip (to the lava column) — about 30 min

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/3.source_en: Lava-tube formation talk at the information center — about 10 min

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/0.source_en: **UNESCO World Natural Heritage 2007** — inscribed under 'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' alongside ⟦G0⟧

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/1.source_en: **Two World Natural Heritage sites in one day** — ⟦G0⟧ + Manjanggul

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/2.source_en: Total length about **7.4 km**, open section about **1 km** (about 30–45 min round trip)

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/3.source_en: **World's largest lava column, 7.6 m high**, at the end of the open section

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/4.source_en: Main passage **18 m wide · 23–25 m high** — one of the world's largest lava tubes

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/5.source_en: **Geomunoreum Lava-Tube System** — formed about 8,000 years ago, a National Natural Monument

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/6.source_en: Interior **11–13°C year-round** — a summer cool-down, jacket recommended

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/7.source_en: Admission **₩4,000 adult / ₩2,000 teens and children**, hours **09:00–18:00 (last entry 17:10)**

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Bring a jacket even in summer (interior 11–13°C). The floor is damp and dark, so non-slip shoes are best. The cave can close for maintenance, so check whether it is operating on your visit date in advance.

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: The information center beside the entrance parking lot explains how the lava tube formed — we recommend a 10-minute look before entering. There is no shop inside the cave.

/itineraryStops/6/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The day's second UNESCO World Natural Heritage site and its natural finale.** After ⟦G0⟧ (a triple-UNESCO tuff cone) and the haenyeo diving performance (intangible heritage), Manjanggul in Gimnyeong sits naturally on the route back from Seongsan to Jeju City. Because it is part of the **same single 2007 inscription** as ⟦G0⟧, pairing the two in one day completes the UNESCO 'Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' narrative. Placing it in the late afternoon **avoids the midday heat and group crowds**, and ends the day on a pleasant note in a **cool 11–13°C cave** after the outdoor itinerary. Should Manjanggul be closed for maintenance or weather, we substitute **Micheon Cave at Ilchul Land**, part of the same lava-tube system, to preserve the cave experience.

/itineraryStops/6/convenience/parking.source_en: Free parking lot at the entrance

/itineraryStops/6/convenience/restroom.source_en: Restrooms at the entrance information center
